whatWeDeliverData.heading: What our change management consulting delivers.
whatWeDeliverData.description: One connected program, from assessment to sustainment. Not a deck and a hand-off: at each step we show what we do, what we build with you, and the deliverable you keep, layer by layer.

steps.title: Assessment
steps.how: Diagnostic instruments benchmarked on our Capability Intelligence Platform.
do: Change readiness assessment across leaders, managers and frontline
Stakeholder and impact analysis by group, role and region
Resistance, risk and current-culture mapping
Run through surveys, interviews and focus groups, onsite or virtual
build: A readiness scorecard by group and function
An impact heatmap of who is affected and how much
A risk-and-resistance register with mitigations
The baseline for every metric we track to sustainment

steps.title: Strategy & roadmap
steps.how: Sponsor-first sequencing, structured by our 5A method.
do: Define the change approach, principles and sponsorship model
Sequence and phase the change across teams and geographies
Tie the change to the business case and success measures
Align the sponsor coalition in working sessions
build: A change strategy tied to the business outcome
A phased roadmap from decision to adoption
A sponsorship and governance model with named owners
A success-measures framework and target adoption curve

steps.title: Stakeholders & impact
steps.how: Influence-impact mapping workshops, informed by the Bridges transition model.
do: Segment stakeholders by influence, impact and sentiment
Detail what changes in each role's day-to-day
Design a tailored engagement plan per group
Enable sponsors and managers as change agents
build: A stakeholder map with influence and impact positioning
A role-by-role impact assessment
An engagement plan and RACI per group
A change-agent network with briefing packs

steps.title: Communications
steps.how: A message-house model, with cadence tuned to the change curve.
do: Craft the change narrative and the 'why' per audience
Plan channels, cadence and messengers, leader-led and peer
Sequence messages to the roadmap milestones
Open two-way feedback and Q&A loops
build: A communications strategy and message house
An audience-by-channel content calendar
Ready-to-use emails, decks, FAQs and town-hall kits
A sentiment dashboard to track reception

steps.title: Enablement
steps.how: Blended 70-20-10 learning design with manager coaching.
do: Training needs analysis by role and capability gap
Blended learning: instructor-led, virtual, e-learning and job aids
Manager enablement so leaders coach the change
Hypercare support through go-live
build: A role-based training curriculum and schedule
Learning assets and quick-reference job aids
A manager coaching toolkit
A hypercare and support model for go-live

steps.title: Sustainment
steps.how: Adoption analytics and reinforcement nudges, on a governed review cadence.
do: Track adoption and usage against the target curve
Reinforce with recognition, nudges and refreshers
Review progress with governance on a set cadence
Transfer the capability to internal change owners
build: An adoption dashboard with leading and lagging metrics
A reinforcement plan across recognition and comms
A governance and review rhythm with owners
A sustainment playbook handed to your team

methodData.heading: The Edstellar 5A change management methodology.
methodData.subheading: Our five-step change management method, grounded in proven change models such as Lewin, Kotter and ADKAR, from business decision to adopted, reinforced new ways of working.

steps.title: Assess
steps.description: Read the change, the stakeholders and the culture to define what adoption will take.

steps.title: Analyze
steps.description: Analyze who is affected, the impact on each group and where resistance is likely, using change diagnostics and stakeholder assessments.

steps.title: Architect
steps.description: Architect the change plan: communication, enablement and reinforcement that close the readiness gaps.

steps.title: Activate
steps.description: Activate the rollout: communicate, train and support people through go-live across teams.

steps.title: Advance
steps.description: Measure adoption, reinforce and sustain each cycle, so the change holds rather than fading.

whyCtaData.heading: Ready for change management that your people actually adopt?

items.question: What does change management consulting include?
items.answer: This organizational change management engagement covers your change strategy and case for change, stakeholder and impact assessment, communication and engagement, training and enablement, resistance management, and the adoption metrics and reinforcement that make it stick, all aligned to the business goal.

items.question: How is change management different from project management?
items.answer: Project management delivers the solution on time and on budget. Change management handles the people side of change, making sure people actually adopt it, by managing the stakeholders, communication and reinforcement that turn a delivered project into new ways of working.

items.question: How long does a change management engagement take?
items.answer: It runs alongside the change it supports, from a few weeks for a focused rollout to several months for a large transformation, depending on scale and how many groups are affected.

items.question: Do you deliver the change, not just plan it?
items.answer: Yes. Communication, training and the reinforcement that embeds new ways of working are a core part of the engagement, so the change becomes how people actually work.

items.question: What do we get at the end?
items.answer: A change strategy, a stakeholder and impact map, a communication and engagement plan, an enablement plan and the adoption metrics you own and run.

items.question: What change management model or framework do you use?
items.answer: Every engagement runs on Edstellar's own 5A method. It is grounded in proven change models, Lewin's unfreeze-change-refreeze, Kotter's 8-step process and the ADKAR adoption model, synthesized into one practical approach so your change is handled systematically rather than by the textbook.
